readings.title: The box with no perfect carrots
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Orchard Cooperative offered a discounted box of vegetables with unusual shapes. Initial interest was high, but some buyers stopped ordering because they received more produce than they could use. The cooperative introduced two box sizes and supplied a list of likely contents before orders closed. Waste reported by buyers fell. The manager realised that rescuing vegetables from rejection at the farm was only part of the task. If the same food was later discarded in a kitchen, the problem had moved rather than disappeared. Quantity and planning mattered alongside acceptance of imperfect appearance.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

readings.title: A kitchen's measuring week
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A workplace kitchen wanted to reduce leftovers but lacked a clear picture of what was being wasted. For one week, staff recorded separate amounts from preparation, unsold meals and diners' plates. The largest share came from meals prepared late in the lunch period. The kitchen began cooking smaller final batches while warning customers that the full menu might not remain available until closing. Waste decreased, though waiting times needed attention. The figures helped the team choose a specific change instead of assuming that diners alone were responsible for every item in the waste bin.

readings.title: The meaning of a local label
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: A market stall described all its products as local, but one customer noticed fruit that could not grow nearby in winter. The seller explained that 'local' referred to the business, not necessarily to every product's origin. To prevent confusion, the stall began displaying the growing region beside each item and describing the business separately. Some customers still chose distant produce; others preferred seasonal alternatives. The change did not tell shoppers what to buy. It gave them a clearer basis for decisions. A familiar, positive word had proved less informative than a precise explanation.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

readings.title: Neighbours cooking together
readings.instruction: Read the original simulation passage and choose the best answer to each question.
readings.content: Residents in a block of flats organised a monthly meal using ingredients left from the week's shopping. The first invitation simply asked everyone to bring 'anything spare'. This produced plenty of bread but few ingredients for a main dish. The next month, one volunteer collected a list in advance and suggested combinations. Participants still chose what to contribute, and nobody was expected to buy extra food. The meal became easier to prepare and remained inexpensive. Organisers also asked about dietary needs before planning. Cooperation worked better when generosity was supported by a little information.
knowledgePoints: 阅读：主旨、细节、推断与语境词义

translation.stem:
Translate the following original passage into Chinese. Preserve the meaning and logical relationships.

The appearance of a vegetable tells us little about the effort used to grow it. Food that looks unusual may still be suitable for a meal. Reducing waste requires better planning as well as a change in expectations. Buying only what we can use is a small but useful beginning.
translation.referenceAnswer: 蔬菜的外观很难告诉我们种植它付出了多少努力。样子不寻常的食物仍然可能适合做成一餐。减少浪费既需要更好的计划，也需要改变期望。只购买能够用完的食物，是一个虽小却有用的开端。
translation.explanation: 参考译文仅示范一种表达。评分时关注信息完整性、转折和条件等逻辑关系；意思准确且中文自然的其他译法同样有效。

writing.stem:
Write an English response of about 120 words to the following original simulation task. Use your own examples and organise your ideas clearly.

Describe a plan for reducing food waste in a local market. Explain how sellers and buyers could cooperate and how success could be measured.
writing.sampleAnswer: A local market could reduce food waste by helping sellers plan late-day sales and helping buyers purchase realistic quantities. Stalls might display discounted produce in smaller mixed bags, with contents clearly listed. This would make unusual-looking vegetables useful to households without giving them more than they can eat. Buyers could be encouraged to bring a short shopping plan and suitable containers. The market should measure unsold edible food before and after the trial, rather than relying only on the number of bags sold. A brief customer survey could also ask whether the food was actually used. Success would mean less waste across the whole journey from stall to kitchen, not simply moving unwanted food from one place to another.
writing.explanation: 范文供完成作答后对照。允许不同立场与例子；围绕题目要求论述清楚、理由充分、语言准确即可。

criteria.description: 结构清楚，信息顺序合理，句段衔接自然，格式符合写作目的。

criteria.description: 词汇使用恰当，句式基本准确，表达清晰；错误按其对理解的影响扣分。
